name: SKUvet Product Feed Check for WooCommerce
author: hieu10x

sections.description:
Feed plugins send whatever your products contain. When a product has no image, no price, no description, no brand or no GTIN, Google Merchant Center and Meta disapprove or limit it, and you find out days later in a diagnostics screen.

SKUvet reads your published products and lists exactly which ones are missing:

  • an image or a price (Google and Meta reject these),
  • a main image under 500 × 500 pixels (Google disapproves these from 31 January 2027), with each image’s size,
  • a price on a variation (each variation is its own feed item),
  • a description,
  • a brand (WooCommerce Brands, common brand plugins, or a “brand” attribute),
  • a GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN (WooCommerce’s own field and the fields of common GTIN and feed plugins) or an MPN,
  • a title of 150 characters or less.

Each problem links to the products so you can fix them. It also names the feed and catalog plugins that are active.

A 72-second walkthrough (demo store, AI voice-over):

It works alongside any feed plugin (Google for WooCommerce, Meta for WooCommerce, Pinterest for WooCommerce, Product Feed PRO, CTX Feed and others). It doesn’t create a feed and doesn’t change your products.

Privacy: the check runs on your own server and reads your own database. Nothing is sent anywhere, and there’s no tracking. The result is stored in one option, removed when you delete the plugin.

This is an early version, built by Hieu Tran with AI agents. A free web version that checks any store from the outside is at https://opsfixes.com/product-feed-check/check/.

SKUvet is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by WooCommerce, Google or Meta.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. Go to WooCommerce → SKUvet and click “Run the check”.
sections.faq:
Which of my products will Google disapprove under the 500×500 image rule?

From 31 January 2027, Google Merchant Center requires product images of at least 500 × 500 pixels and disapproves smaller ones (“Image too small”). SKUvet lists every product, and every variation with its own image, whose main image is under 500 pixels on either side, with the image’s size. Sizes come from the image data WordPress already stores, so nothing is downloaded.

Merchant Center says “Limited performance due to missing identifiers”. Which products is it?

SKUvet lists the products with no GTIN (UPC, EAN, ISBN) and no MPN, and the products with no brand, with links to edit them. Whether Google needs identifiers depends on the product and the country; products that truly have none (handmade, vintage) are listed too, so you can decide.

Does it change my products or my feed?

No. It only reads products and shows what’s missing.

My feed plugin adds GTINs from its own field. Will it see them?

It reads WooCommerce’s GTIN field and the fields used by common GTIN and feed plugins. If your plugin stores GTINs somewhere else, they won’t be seen; use your feed plugin’s preview to confirm.

How many products can it check?

Up to 5,000 published products per run.
